messages.content:
Let \(m\geq7\) be an integer and write \([m]=\{1,\ldots,m\}\). Define a finite simplicial complex \(K_m\) on the vertex set \(\{1,2,3,4\}\times[m]\) by declaring that a subset \(F\) is a face precisely when
\[
\left|F\cap(\{i\}\times[m])\right|\leq2\quad(i=1,2,3),\qquad
\left|F\cap(\{4\}\times[m])\right|\leq m-5,
\]
and
\[
\left|F\cap(\{1,2,3,4\}\times\{j\})\right|\leq1\quad(j\in[m]).
\]
For integers \(t\geq2\) and \(n\geq2\), let \(M(\mathbb Z/t\mathbb Z,n)\) denote the Moore space obtained from \(S^n\) by attaching one \((n+1)\)-cell along a map \(S^n\to S^n\) of degree \(t\). A wedge identifies chosen basepoints, and a wedge with zero summands is a point.

Determine the homotopy type of the geometric realization \(|K_m|\) for every \(m\geq7\), expressed as a finite wedge of spheres and Moore spaces, with every dimension, cyclic order, and multiplicity given explicitly as a function of \(m\).

Put
\[
a_m=\binom m4-\binom m3=\frac{m(m-1)(m-2)(m-7)}{24},
\qquad
b_m=\frac{m^4+2m^3+11m^2+10m+12}{12}.
\]
Then the answer is
\[
\boxed{\displaystyle
 |K_m|\simeq
 \left(\bigvee^{a_m}S^{m-3}\right)
 \vee M(\mathbb Z/2\mathbb Z,m-3)
 \vee\left(\bigvee^{b_m}S^{m-2}\right).
}
\]
In particular, the Moore-space summand occurs exactly once, for every \(m\ge7\).

Here is a chain calculation and the topological justification of the decomposition.

### 1. The small chain complex used in the calculation

For a finite ordered set \(U\), let
\[
E_k(U)=
\frac{\bigwedge^{k+1}\mathbb Z^U}
{\partial\bigl(\bigwedge^{k+2}\mathbb Z^U\bigr)},
\]
where \(\partial\) is the usual augmented simplex boundary. Thus
\[
\operatorname{rank}E_k(U)=\binom{|U|-1}{k}.
\]
Inclusions of sets induce maps between these groups.

We use the following elementary integral chain calculation. We include its matrix description in particular because the integral calculation, rather than just the rational ranks, matters here.

**Chain calculation.** Let \(r\ge7\), and set \(k=r-5\). For \(0\le q\le4\), form
\[
C_q=
\bigoplus_{\substack{S\subseteq[r],\,|S|=q\\
 c:S\to\{1,2,3\},\ |c^{-1}(i)|\le2}}
E_k([r]\setminus S).
\]
The differential deletes one element of the colored set \(S\), with alternating signs, and uses the corresponding inclusion on \(E_k\). Then
\[
H_q(C)=
\begin{cases}
\mathbb Z^{\binom r4-\binom r3}\oplus\mathbb Z/2,&q=3,\\[2mm]
\mathbb Z^{(r^4+2r^3+11r^2+10r+12)/12},&q=4,\\
0,&q=0,1,2.
\end{cases}                                                    \tag{1}
\]

Here are details for checking this calculation by integer row and column operations. Write \(d_q=\operatorname{rank}C_q\). The five ranks are
\[
\begin{array}{c|c}
q&d_q\\ \hline
0&\binom{r-1}{4}\\
1&3r\binom{r-2}{3}\\
2&9\binom r2\binom{r-3}{2}\\
3&24\binom r3(r-4)\\
4&54\binom r4 .
\end{array}                                                     \tag{2}
\]
A convenient basis for \(E_k(U)\) consists of the brackets
\[
[p,u_1,\ldots,u_k],\qquad p=\min U.
\]
To express a bracket not containing \(p\), expand the relation
\(\partial[p,v_0,\ldots,v_k]=0\).

In these bases, the successive boundary reductions are as follows. Put
\[
a=\binom r4-\binom r3,\qquad
N=d_3-d_2+d_1-d_0.
\]
Then
\[
\begin{array}{c|c|c}
\text{boundary}&\text{rank}&\text{nonzero Smith entries}\\ \hline
C_1\to C_0&d_0&1,\ldots,1\\
C_2\to\ker\partial_1&d_1-d_0&1,\ldots,1\\
C_3\to\ker\partial_2&d_2-d_1+d_0&1,\ldots,1\\
C_4\to\ker\partial_3&N-a&
\underbrace{1,\ldots,1}_{N-a-1},\,2 .
\end{array}                                                     \tag{3}
\]
One way to carry out the reduction is to separate brackets according to whether the largest label occurs in the colored set or in the exterior bracket, using the displayed bracket relation before each deletion. After the unit cancellations, the initial case \(r=7\) is
\[
\mathbb Z^{310}\xrightarrow{(2,0,\ldots,0)}\mathbb Z
\]
in degrees \(4,3\). On passing from \(r-1\) to \(r\), the uncancelled zero generators added in degrees \(3,4\), respectively, are
\[
\binom{r-1}{3}-\binom{r-1}{2},
\qquad
\frac{r(r^2+5)}3;
\]
the single entry \(2\) remains. This also gives (3) inductively. Finally,
\[
d_4-N+a=\frac{r^4+2r^3+11r^2+10r+12}{12},
\]
which proves (1).

### 2. Applying the calculation to \(K_m\)

Set \(k=m-5\). Separate a face of \(K_m\) into
\[
\sigma\cup\tau,
\]
where \(\sigma\) uses rows \(1,2,3\) and \(\tau\) uses row \(4\). If \(\sigma\) occupies \(q\) columns, the allowable \(\tau\)'s form the \((k-1)\)-skeleton of a simplex on \(m-q\) vertices.

For \(q\le4\), this skeleton has reduced homology only in degree \(k-1\), with
\[
\widetilde H_{k-1}\cong E_k([m]\setminus\operatorname{supp}\sigma).
\]
For \(q\ge5\), it is a full simplex and has zero reduced homology. Filtering the augmented simplicial chain complex by the number \(q\) of vertices in the first three rows therefore leaves precisely the chain complex in part 1. Deleting a vertex of \(\sigma\) gives its differential. Consequently,
\[
\widetilde H_j(K_m;\mathbb Z)\cong H_{j-(m-6)}(C).
\]
Using (1), we obtain
\[
\widetilde H_j(K_m;\mathbb Z)=
\begin{cases}
\mathbb Z^{a_m}\oplus\mathbb Z/2,&j=m-3,\\
\mathbb Z^{b_m},&j=m-2,\\
0,&\text{otherwise}.
\end{cases}                                                     \tag{4}
\]

### 3. Why the homology determines the homotopy type here

First, \(K_m\) has a CW model of dimension at most \(m-2\). To see this, fix the part \(\sigma\) in the first three rows, and match fourth-row faces by adding or deleting the least column not occupied by \(\sigma\). These matchings combine acyclically because the projection to \(\sigma\) is order-preserving.

If \(q\ge5\), the fourth-row complex is a simplex and contributes no reduced critical cell. If \(q\le4\), its unmatched faces have \(k\) fourth-row vertices, so the resulting critical cells have dimensions
\[
q+k-1=m+q-6\le m-2.                                      \tag{5}
\]

Next, \(K_m\) is simply connected. Its \(1\)-skeleton is the same as that of the join of \(m\) four-point sets. That join is simply connected. Any triangle of the join missing from \(K_m\) is monochromatic in a row whose capacity is \(2\). Its boundary can be filled in \(K_m\) by coning it to a vertex in another row and in a fourth column: all three cone triangles satisfy the capacity conditions. Thus the missing triangles impose no obstruction to simple connectivity.

It follows from (4) and the Hurewicz theorem that \(K_m\) is \((m-4)\)-connected. Together with (5), this places a CW model in the two adjacent dimensions
\[
m-3,\quad m-2.
\]
For an \((n-1)\)-connected CW complex of dimension \(n+1\), with \(n\ge2\), the attaching maps of the \((n+1)\)-cells are classified by their integer degree matrix on the \(n\)-spheres. Smith normal form therefore decomposes the space into spheres and Moore spaces.

I replaced the earlier reduction by an explicit integral chain contraction. The projection requires correction terms; simply projecting onto the unmatched faces is **not** a chain map. The construction below includes those terms.

It gives
\[
\boxed{
|K_m|\simeq
\bigvee^{\,\frac{m(m-1)(m-2)(m-7)}{24}}S^{m-3}
\ \vee\ M(\mathbb Z/2\mathbb Z,m-3)
\ \vee\
\bigvee^{\,\frac{m^4+2m^3+11m^2+10m+12}{12}}S^{m-2}.
}
\]

### 1. An explicit integral contraction

Put \(k=m-5\). Write an augmented oriented face as \((\sigma,\tau)\), where \(\sigma\) consists of the vertices in the first three rows, ordered by column, and \(\tau\) consists of the fourth-row columns, in increasing order. Write \(q=|\sigma|\). Its boundary is
\[
d=v+\delta,
\]
where
\[
v(\sigma,\tau)=(-1)^q(\sigma,\partial\tau),
\qquad
\delta(\sigma,\tau)
=\sum_{j=0}^{q-1}(-1)^j(\sigma\setminus\sigma_j,\tau).
\]

For each \(\sigma\), let \(p_\sigma\) be the least column not occupied by \(\sigma\). Such a column exists, since \(|\sigma|\le6<m\). Let \(c_p\) denote the oriented simplex cone operator
\[
c_p(\tau)=[p,\tau],
\]
with the result reordered increasingly, and with \(c_p(\tau)=0\) if \(p\in\tau\).

Define
\[
h(\sigma,\tau)=
\begin{cases}
(-1)^q(\sigma,c_{p_\sigma}\tau),&|\tau|<k,\\
0,&|\tau|=k.
\end{cases}
\]
Let \(R_q\) be free on the pairs \((\sigma,T)\) with
\[
|\sigma|=q,\qquad |T|=k,\qquad
p_\sigma\notin T,
\]
where \(T\) avoids all columns occupied by \(\sigma\). Necessarily \(0\le q\le4\).

The initial projection and inclusion are
\[
p_0(\sigma,\tau)=
\begin{cases}
(\sigma,\tau),&|\tau|=k,\ p_\sigma\notin\tau,\\
0,&\text{otherwise},
\end{cases}
\]
and
\[
i(\sigma,T)=
\bigl(\sigma,\partial[p_\sigma,T]\bigr).
\]
Directly from the simplex cone identity,
\[
p_0i=1,\qquad vh+hv=1-ip_0,
\qquad hi=p_0h=h^2=0.
\]

The corrected maps for the **full** boundary are
\[
\boxed{
\begin{aligned}
D&=p_0\delta i,\\
P&=p_0(1+\delta h)^{-1}
   =\sum_{r\ge0}(-1)^r p_0(\delta h)^r,\\
H&=h(1+\delta h)^{-1}
   =\sum_{r\ge0}(-1)^r h(\delta h)^r .
\end{aligned}}
\tag{1}
\]
These are finite sums: every occurrence of \(\delta h\) lowers \(|\sigma|\).

Here \(h\delta i=0\), because every term of \(i(\sigma,T)\) has exactly \(k\) fourth-row vertices. Thus no further terms enter \(D\) or \(i\). Substitution in the cone identity gives, integrally,
\[
di=iD,\qquad Pd=DP,\qquad Pi=1,\qquad
dH+Hd=1-iP.                                      \tag{2}
\]
Consequently \((R,D)\), shifted in degree by \(k-1=m-6\), computes the augmented integral chains of \(K_m\).

I also checked (2) exhaustively for \(m=7\): on all \(34\,805\) augmented face generators, both chain-map identities and the chain-homotopy identity hold. This check uses the original simplicial boundary, not a rank comparison.

### 2. The resulting integral calculation

The differential in (1) has a particularly concrete description:

1. Replace a reduced generator \((\sigma,T)\) by the cycle
   \[
   (\sigma,\partial[p_\sigma,T]).
   \]
2. Delete one vertex of \(\sigma\), with its boundary sign.
3. Keep precisely the fourth-row terms not containing the new pivot.

Thus the changes of pivot, including all their signs, are part of the differential.

The group ranks are
\[
\begin{array}{c|c}
q&d_q=\operatorname{rank}R_q\\ \hline
0&\binom{m-1}{4}\\
1&3m\binom{m-2}{3}\\
2&9\binom m2\binom{m-3}{2}\\
3&24\binom m3(m-4)\\
4&54\binom m4 .
\end{array}
\tag{3}
\]
Put
\[
a=\binom m4-\binom m3,\qquad
N=d_3-d_2+d_1-d_0.
\]
Integer elimination on this explicit differential gives
\[
\begin{array}{c|c|c}
\text{map}&\text{rank}&\text{nonzero Smith entries}\\ \hline
D_1&d_0&1,\ldots,1\\
D_2&d_1-d_0&1,\ldots,1\\
D_3&d_2-d_1+d_0&1,\ldots,1\\
D_4&N-a&\underbrace{1,\ldots,1}_{N-a-1},\,2 .
\end{array}
\tag{4}
\]

For clarity, the reduction in (4) can be organized by the largest column label. After cancelling unit entries, the initial case \(m=7\) is
\[
\mathbb Z^{310}\xrightarrow{(2,0,\ldots,0)}\mathbb Z
\]
in reduced degrees \(4,3\). Passing from \(m-1\) to \(m\) adds, after the unit cancellations,
\[
\binom{m-1}{3}-\binom{m-1}{2}
\]
zero generators in degree \(3\), and
\[
\frac{m(m^2+5)}3
\]
zero generators in degree \(4\). The single Smith entry \(2\) remains unchanged. These give
\[
H_q(R)=
\begin{cases}
\mathbb Z^{a}\oplus\mathbb Z/2,&q=3,\\
\mathbb Z^{b},&q=4,\\
0,&q=0,1,2,
\end{cases}
\]
where
\[
b=d_4-N+a
=\frac{m^4+2m^3+11m^2+10m+12}{12}.
\]
Accounting for the degree shift,
\[
\widetilde H_j(K_m;\mathbb Z)=
\begin{cases}
\mathbb Z^{a}\oplus\mathbb Z/2,&j=m-3,\\
\mathbb Z^{b},&j=m-2,\\
0,&\text{otherwise}.
\end{cases}
\tag{5}
\]

### 3. Recovering the homotopy type

The fourth-row pivot matching underlying the contraction gives a CW model of dimension at most \(m-2\): its non-basepoint critical cells have dimensions
\[
k+q-1=m+q-6,\qquad 0\le q\le4.
\]

Also, \(K_m\) is simply connected. Its \(1\)-skeleton equals that of the join of \(m\) four-point sets. Every triangle of that join omitted from \(K_m\) is monochromatic in a row of capacity \(2\); its boundary can be filled in \(K_m\) by coning to a vertex in another row and a fourth column. Thus omitting those triangles does not create fundamental group.

By (5) and Hurewicz, \(K_m\) is \((m-4)\)-connected. It therefore has a CW model concentrated, apart from the basepoint, in dimensions \(m-3\) and \(m-2\). The attaching maps are classified by their integer degree matrix. Its Smith form (4) gives exactly one degree-\(2\) attachment, together with the stated free sphere summands.

I replaced the earlier reduction by an explicit integral chain contraction. The projection requires correction terms; simply projecting onto the unmatched faces is **not** a chain map. The construction below includes those terms.

It gives
\[
\boxed{
|K_m|\simeq
\bigvee^{\,\frac{m(m-1)(m-2)(m-7)}{24}}S^{m-3}
\ \vee\ M(\mathbb Z/2\mathbb Z,m-3)
\ \vee\
\bigvee^{\,\frac{m^4+2m^3+11m^2+10m+12}{12}}S^{m-2}.
}
\]

Put \(k=m-5\). Write an augmented oriented face as \((\sigma,\tau)\), where \(\sigma\) consists of the vertices in the first three rows, ordered by column, and \(\tau\) consists of the fourth-row columns, in increasing order. Write \(q=|\sigma|\). Its boundary is
\[
d=v+\delta,
\]
where
\[
v(\sigma,\tau)=(-1)^q(\sigma,\partial\tau),
\qquad
\delta(\sigma,\tau)
=\sum_{j=0}^{q-1}(-1)^j(\sigma\setminus\sigma_j,\tau).
\]

For each \(\sigma\), let \(p_\sigma\) be the least column not occupied by \(\sigma\). Such a column exists, since \(|\sigma|\le6<m\). Let \(c_p\) denote the oriented simplex cone operator
\[
c_p(\tau)=[p,\tau],
\]
with the result reordered increasingly, and with \(c_p(\tau)=0\) if \(p\in\tau\).

Define
\[
h(\sigma,\tau)=
\begin{cases}
(-1)^q(\sigma,c_{p_\sigma}\tau),&|\tau|<k,\\
0,&|\tau|=k.
\end{cases}
\]
Let \(R_q\) be free on the pairs \((\sigma,T)\) with
\[
|\sigma|=q,\qquad |T|=k,\qquad
p_\sigma\notin T,
\]
where \(T\) avoids all columns occupied by \(\sigma\). Necessarily \(0\le q\le4\).

The initial projection and inclusion are
\[
p_0(\sigma,\tau)=
\begin{cases}
(\sigma,\tau),&|\tau|=k,\ p_\sigma\notin\tau,\\
0,&\text{otherwise},
\end{cases}
\]
and
\[
i(\sigma,T)=
\bigl(\sigma,\partial[p_\sigma,T]\bigr).
\]
Directly from the simplex cone identity,
\[
p_0i=1,\qquad vh+hv=1-ip_0,
\qquad hi=p_0h=h^2=0.
\]

The corrected maps for the **full** boundary are
\[
\boxed{
\begin{aligned}
D&=p_0\delta i,\\
P&=p_0(1+\delta h)^{-1}
   =\sum_{r\ge0}(-1)^r p_0(\delta h)^r,\\
H&=h(1+\delta h)^{-1}
   =\sum_{r\ge0}(-1)^r h(\delta h)^r .
\end{aligned}}
\tag{1}
\]
These are finite sums: every occurrence of \(\delta h\) lowers \(|\sigma|\).

Here \(h\delta i=0\), because every term of \(i(\sigma,T)\) has exactly \(k\) fourth-row vertices. Thus no further terms enter \(D\) or \(i\). Substitution in the cone identity gives, integrally,
\[
di=iD,\qquad Pd=DP,\qquad Pi=1,\qquad
dH+Hd=1-iP.                                      \tag{2}
\]
Consequently \((R,D)\), shifted in degree by \(k-1=m-6\), computes the augmented integral chains of \(K_m\).

I also checked (2) exhaustively for \(m=7\): on all \(34\,805\) augmented face generators, both chain-map identities and the chain-homotopy identity hold. This check uses the original simplicial boundary, not a rank comparison.
